newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude futures correct mildly upwards.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude futures correct mildly upwards.

text.p: IPE Brent futures strengthened slightly on Thursday to correct some of the previous day's sharp fall but the rise was half-hearted, dealers said.
At 1430 gmt August Brent crude was at $17.85 a barrel, eight cents up on the day. In New York the front month NYMEX crude contract stood at $18.90 a barrel, 11 cents better than yesterday's close.

"We are slightly stronger after yesterday's break downwards and its a little bit of a correction from those strong falls," said one dealer. August Brent closed 31 cents down on Wednesday after bearish sentiment through the market.
The expected boost from NYMEX business failed to materialise, with early New York trade dampening some spirited buying in London.
"We appear to be confined to a bit of a range at the moment. Yesterday we tested the bottom of that and now we're back up a little," said one dealer.
Upside targets for Brent and NYMEX crude were pegged at $18.00 and $19.00 respectively, with more substantial resistance for the North Sea benchmark at $18.15 and then $18.30 a barrel.
IPE July gas oil was up just 50 cents at 14.30 gmt at $159.25 a tonne in directionless trade, dealers said.

With the market fundamentally weakened by over-supply, the threat of a further delay in the resumption of crude exports from Iraq under Baghdad's oil-for-food deal with the U.N. was providing the only relief from downward pressure.
But worries over Iraq were marginal, some brokers said, and the continuing contango was the best reflection of bearishness on crude prices.
Gas oil paper was seen under continued pressure from Russian supplies hitting the physical market, which has also been badly affected by the tightly shut arb windows to the U.S. and Asia.
